Sure! If your DNS provider exposes a RESTful API that lets you filter the fields you receive, you can usually do this in one of two ways: | Method | What you do | Example | |--------|-------------|---------| | **Query‑string field selector** | Append a `fields=` parameter listing only the attributes you want. | `GET https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context` | | **JSON‑body projection** | Send a JSON body with a `projection` or `select` key that lists the fields. | `POST https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records`
Body: `{ "type": "CAA", "projection": ["id", "context"] }` | Below is a quick, language‑agnostic example using `curl`. Replace `https://api.dnsprovider.com` with your provider’s base URL and `secret567` with your actual API key. ```bash # Using the query‑string selector curl -X GET \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` If your provider prefers a POST with a projection body, try: ```bash curl -X POST \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "type": "CAA", "projection": ["id", "context"] }' ``` ### Things to double‑check 1. **Field names** – Some APIs use `id` and `context`, others might use `record_id` or `attributes`. Look at the provider’s docs for the exact field names. 2. **Pagination** – If there are many records, the API may paginate. Add `page=1&per_page=100` (or whatever the provider uses) to get all results in one request. 3. **Rate limits** – Keep an eye on the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header if you’re making many calls. ### Example response ```json [ { "id": "caacb1d2-3e4f-5678-9abc-0123456789ab", "context": { "issue": "letsencrypt.org", "iodef": "mailto:security@example.com" } }, { "id": "caacb1d2-3e4f-5678-9abc-0123456789ac", "context": { "issue": "digicert.com" } } ] ``` That’s it—just the IDs and the context attributes, nothing else. Happy querying!
